 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV) No.1793/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 03/07/2019.
The sole respondent herein is 2nd respondent/insurer in the petition.

In this appeal,
the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.
2. The claim petitioners are the parents and sister of deceased Alex.

According to the claimants, on 24/07/2016 at 08:30 p.m., while Alex was riding his motor cycle bearing reg. no.KL-41/G 5986 through Marampilly- South Vazhakulam Road, 2025:KER:40043 a Tata Ace bearing reg.
no.KL-7/BP 4302 driven by the 1 st respondent negligently, knocked him down due to which he sustained serious injuries to which he succumbed on the same day.
3. The 1st respondent, the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle remained ex parte.
4. The 2nd respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
It was contended that there was no negligence on the part of the 1st respondent and that the accident was due to the negligence of the deceased.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A10 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner No documentary evidence was produced by the 2nd respondent.

6. The Tribunal on a consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found 2025:KER:40043 negligence on the part of the 1st respondent owner cum driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 16,12,400/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal on the following heads are challenged.
Notional income
The learned counsel for the claim petitioners submitted that the deceased was aged 21 years and was an electrician at the time of the incident.
His monthly income was stated to be 20,000/-.

The Tribunal fixed the notional income at 9,500/-
2025:KER:40043 which is quite low and therefore, the same needs to be interfered with and reasonably enhanced.

The learned counsel for the claim petitioners submits that even going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited, (2011) 13 SCC 236, the notional income of a coolie in the year 2016 is liable to be fixed at 10,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case,
the deceased was an electrician and therefore, appropriate increase in the amount may be made.

The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/insurer opposes the submission and submits that the amount that has been fixed is quite reasonable and if at all any enhancement is required, it may be as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra).
Going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income of a coolie is liable to be fixed at 10,500/- in the year 2016.
The specific pleading is to the effect that the deceased was a business man and not an electrician.
It is true that Ext.A10 has been produced which is a certificate issued by the 2025:KER:40043 Principal, Skiltek, Private Industrial Training Institute, Kochi.
In these circumstances, I find that fixing an amount of 12,000/- as notional income would be reasonable.
Love and affection

The learned counsel for the claim petitioners fairly conceded that award of 50,000/- as compensation towards loss of love and affection is incorrect as compensation towards 'loss of consortium' has been granted.

In the light of the dictums in Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram, (2018) 18 SCC 130: 2018 KHC 6697, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur, AIR 2020 SC 3076: 2023 KHC 760 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Somwati, 2020 KHC 6530 : (2020) 9 SCC 644, the compensation that has been awarded by the Tribunal for 'loss of love and affection' as well as loss of consortium is apparently incorrect.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 3,28,000/- (total compensation 19,40,400/- that is, 16,12,400/-
granted by the Tribunal + 3,28,000/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization and proportionate costs.
The 2nd respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioners at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
